# Rules (project-local layer)

These `.md` files are the **base rules** that `/dotclaude:init` scaffolds into your project. Claude Code loads them automatically, extending `CLAUDE.md` without bloating it.

- `alwaysApply: true` — loaded every session. Keep it tight (under ~30 lines).
- `paths: [...]` — loaded only when you're working near matching files.

## Ownership

A file carrying a `dotclaude:managed` marker (an HTML comment right after the frontmatter) is owned by the dotclaude base, and `/dotclaude:init` overwrites it on update. To take local ownership of one, **delete its marker line** — dotclaude then leaves it alone. Any rule file you add without a marker is yours and is never touched.

The base ships `code-quality`, `testing`, and `pr-review` (always-on), plus `security`, `error-handling`, `frontend`, and `database` (path-scoped). Delete the ones that don't fit your stack, or adjust their `paths:` globs. The always-on rules also generate the repo-wide `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, so the PR review discipline applies to Copilot too.

## Adding your own

Create a new `.md` file here with `alwaysApply: true` or `paths: [...]` frontmatter. Don't add the managed marker — leaving it off signals the file is yours. See the [Claude Code docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory#path-specific-rules).
